Configure the nuget client to use Repsy

Configure the nuget client to use a Repsy repository.

rp edits the client's own configuration file; it never replaces it. Every file
that would change is shown as a diff first, you confirm each write (--yes
skips the question), and the original is kept next to it as a timestamped
backup. A second run changes nothing.

--scope selects what is written. The default is user (your home directory).
nuget supports: user (.nuget/NuGet/NuGet.Config), project (nuget.config). An unsupported scope is an error; rp never writes
somewhere else instead.

The token is NOT written to the file by default. rp writes a reference, %REPSY_TOKEN%, so that the client reads the token from the
environment variable REPSY_TOKEN when it runs.
--embed-token writes the plain token instead; the file then holds a secret,
and rp warns about it. Use it only when the client cannot read the environment.

With --repo, rp first checks that the repository exists (one request, also
with --dry-run and --print) and stops with an error before it writes anything
when it does not.

--dry-run shows the diff and writes nothing; --print shows the complete new
file (secrets redacted) and writes nothing. Neither runs a command.

If you answer no to a question, that change is skipped and rp still exits 0; the
messages on stderr say what was not done.

```
rp nuget setup [flags]
```

## Options

```
      --dry-run        Show the diff and write nothing
      --embed-token    Write the plain token into the file instead of an environment variable reference (unsafe: the file then holds a secret)
      --print          Print the complete new file content (secrets redacted) and write nothing
      --repo string    Repository to configure the client for
      --scope string   Where to write: user (your home directory) or project (the working directory) (default "user")
```
